segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, um.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, welcome back, this is our second meeting, the functional design one.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Uh, first thing, Tom isn't here today.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh, is he okay?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, he messaged me this morning, he's got a doctor's appointment he couldn't move.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Ah, okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So it's just the three of us.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um, I sent round the minutes from the kickoff, I hope you both got them.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yep, got them.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Good. So the agenda, uh, Priya will present the interface, then Marcus the working design.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And then we really need to decide clip or wristband, because we put that off last time.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Tom's research on the existing step counters, we'll have to, um, leave that for now.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh, and one more thing before we start.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Last time we said someone should check the whole cost, the strap, the packaging, everything, against the fifteen euros.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And nobody actually took that on.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Right, yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Priya, could you maybe do that one?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, yeah, I mean.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I can try, I don't really know the part prices but I can look them up.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Great, thanks. Okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Priya, do you want to go first?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, sure. Um, so I looked at the display and the buttons.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And I made a few rough sketches, I'll just pass them round.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So the main thing, like we agreed, is the step count, really big.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I'd say the digits about two centimetres high, so you can read it without your glasses.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Mm, that's good, yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Two centimetres, how many digits is that?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Five digits, so up to ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, that's a fairly wide screen then.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, it's about five centimetres across.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, then functions. I tried to keep it really minimal.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Number one, the steps today. Number two, a little bar that shows how far you are to your daily goal.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And that's it, basically.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And how do you switch between those?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: One button. One big button on the front. You press it and it goes from steps to the goal bar and back.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And the count resets by itself at midnight, so there's no reset button at all.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Oh, I like that. Less to break.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, someone pressing reset by accident and losing the whole day, that'd be annoying.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Exactly, that was the idea.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: What about the daily goal though, who sets that?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, I thought fixed at six thousand steps, out of the box.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Because a settings menu with one button, that gets complicated really fast.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, true.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, fixed goal, I think that's fine for now.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And, uh, one more idea, a backlight. When you press the button it lights up for a few seconds.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: For when it's a bit dark, in the evening.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Hmm, um.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That'll eat into the battery though, I'll get to that.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let's hold that thought until Marcus has done his part.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah. That's all from me really.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Thanks Priya, that's really clear.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Marcus?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah. So, um, the working design.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: For the sensor I'd go with a three-axis accelerometer, it's the standard thing, they're really cheap now, under a euro.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And it works at the hip and on the wrist, technically both are possible.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: But, um, here's the thing I found about the wrist.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: On the wrist it counts your arm swinging. And a lot of seniors walk with a rollator, or a stick, or they're pushing a shopping trolley.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And then the arm doesn't swing, so the wristband just misses loads of steps.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Ah, so for someone with a walker it would basically show nothing.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Pretty much, yeah, it really undercounts. At the hip you don't have that problem.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Hmm, that's quite a strong argument actually.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And then the battery. Like I said last time, a coin cell, a CR2032.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: With a simple LCD, no backlight, that runs for about a year.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And with Priya's backlight?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Depends how often you press it, but you could lose maybe a third of that, maybe more.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Hmm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And the display, a plain segment LCD, black digits on grey, that's cheap, maybe a euro fifty at that size.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Uh, and I've got rough prices for all the parts already, the sensor, the chip, the battery, the case.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's mostly it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, so.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let's do the big one then, clip or wristband.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Priya, you were for the wristband last time, how do you feel after hearing that?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: The rollator thing, yeah, that kind of changes it for me.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: My only worry was always that the clip is fiddly, like with stiff fingers, getting it on your belt.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: We can make the clip big, a wide spring clip, you just push it over the waistband.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, if it's big enough, okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And maybe a little safety cord, so if it slips off it doesn't fall on the floor.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: A cord's cheap, that's a few cents.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let's see if it fits in the cost though, we'll leave the cord open for now.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So we go with the clip at the hip, everybody agree?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yes, from my side definitely.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, okay, clip.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, clip it is.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Then the backlight.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Well, um.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: If it costs a third of the battery maybe it's not worth it.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I'd leave it out, honestly, the digits are big anyway.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, so no backlight, we keep the one-year battery.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, fine.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And the fall detection Tom wanted, is that still parked?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Marcus, could the sensor even do that?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: The accelerometer could detect a fall, sort of, but then you need an alarm, and to call someone you need a phone link or a base station.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's way over fifteen euros.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Then I'd say we take it off the list for this product.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, makes sense.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'll tell Tom, I know he liked the idea.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, the cost check.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Actually, since I already have the part prices, maybe it's easier if I do the total?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh, yes please, honestly, that'd be much quicker.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, that makes more sense. So Marcus does the cost check, Priya, you're off that one.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Thanks.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I'll add the clip, the packaging, the battery, all of it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Then Tom. He still owes us the research on existing step counters, so that moves to the next meeting.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And I want him to find out whether seniors would actually wear a clip, whether they'd accept it at the hip.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, good, because if they hate clips we have a problem.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Exactly. I'll put that in my email to him.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Priya, for the next meeting, could you work out the display and the button for the clip version, the size and where the button sits?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, I can do that.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And Marcus, besides the cost, the case and the clip itself, the materials.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, sure.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'll send the minutes and an email to Tom with his tasks.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: We've still got no name, by the way, but that can wait.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Ha, yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, I think that's it. Thanks both.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Thanks.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Bye.

abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting and noted that the marketing expert was absent because of a doctor's appointment, so his research on existing step counters could not be presented. The user interface designer presented a minimal interface: a large five-digit step count, a daily goal progress bar, one big button to switch between the two, and an automatic reset at midnight. The industrial designer proposed a three-axis accelerometer, a CR2032 coin cell lasting about a year, and a simple segment LCD. He pointed out that a wristband undercounts steps for seniors using a rollator or stick. Based on this, the team decided on a clip worn at the hip. The team dropped the proposed backlight to protect battery life and removed fall detection from the product because of the 15-euro cost limit. The check of the total cost was first given to the user interface designer and then moved to the industrial designer, who already had the part prices.
